installation.note: cal is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The cal command displays a calendar for a specified month or year. It's a simple but useful command for quickly checking dates, planning, or getting calendar information in the terminal. It supports various formats and can show calendars for specific months, years, or date ranges.
when_to_use: Check what day a date falls on

misconceptions.title: cal shows events or holidays
misconceptions.misconception: cal displays holidays, events, or appointments
misconceptions.reality: cal only shows the calendar structure (dates and days). It doesn't show holidays, events, or any additional information.
misconceptions.tip: cal is just a date display tool. For events and holidays, use calendar applications or specialized tools.

misconceptions.title: cal can set reminders
misconceptions.misconception: cal can be used to set calendar reminders or alarms
misconceptions.reality: cal is read-only - it only displays calendars. It cannot set reminders, events, or any calendar data.
misconceptions.tip: cal is for viewing only. Use calendar applications (like GNOME Calendar) for managing events and reminders.

common_pitfalls.solution: Format is 'cal [month] [year]' - month first, then year. Or just 'cal 2024' for full year.

common_pitfalls.description: Some systems accept month names, others only numbers
common_pitfalls.solution: Use month numbers (1-12) for portability: cal 3 2024 (March), not cal march 2024

related_commands.relationship: Date information; date shows current date/time, cal shows calendar
related_commands.description: Display or set the system date and time

best_practices: Use cal for quick date reference in terminal
Use cal -3 for context around current month
Use cal -y for yearly planning overview
Use cal -m for Monday-first week format if preferred
Use month numbers (1-12) for better portability
performance_tips: cal is very fast - negligible performance impact
Year calendars are slightly slower but still instant
No network or file access required - pure calculation

additional_notes.default_week_start: Default is Sunday-first week (US convention). Use -m for Monday-first (ISO 8601).
additional_notes.month_format: Month can be specified as number (1-12) or name, but numbers are more portable
additional_notes.read_only: cal is read-only - it only displays, cannot modify or store calendar data
